text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
- Russian President Yeltsin wants to return soon to Kremlin after heart operation
- Coalition searches for way to get out of tax row. Separate law proposed for the reduction of the solidarity tax. The stumbling block is over the timing of the tax reduction.
- The economic conditions in Germany are iproving. But the upturn is not strong enough to create new jobs, according to DIHT survey of 25,000 companies. Worries about east German economy remain.
- Former RAF guerrilla Birgit Hogefeld sentenced by Frankfurt court to life in prison for her involvement in series of attacks in 1980s.
- Deutsche Telekom initial public offering is four times oversubscribed, company officials say.
- CDU leader Schaeuble warns about possibility of break in coalition and rejects FDP demands for legislation setting up reduction in solidarity tax.
- Kohl says coalition is in good shape. Finance Minister Waigel indicates he is willing to compromise with FDP on solidarity tax dispute.
- Foreign Minister Kinkel criticises the EU's policies towards Turkey, saying it was mistake for EU to stop all EU payments to the EU.
- Coalition grapples with budget row, searches for way out of jam. Chancellor Kohl calls all ministers into chancellery for meeting.
- German post office may have to close 6,500 of its 16,500 branch offices.
